summary: gitdump.py is a stdlib-only .git-directory reconstruction helper — it emits no findings itself. Its output drives the `web-git-dump` finding in recce/services/web/loot.py: parses .git/index, inflates loose objects, mines them for secrets and URL-embedded creds + AWS access keys, and folds recovered credentials into the credential store as `web-git-loot`. This is real T3 (initial access — plaintext creds captured and made sprayable); the finding itself is high-sev with concrete file counts. Packfiles are noted but not delta-resolved (biggest coverage gap — most production git repos have their history packed). Reflog / stash / branch enumeration also absent.

findings.title_pattern: Exposed .git reconstructed - source tree + secrets recovered
findings.tier_evidence: Recovered plaintext blobs, mined real credentials (username+secret dicts), and Credential objects folded into the store with source=web-git-loot — this is direct foothold material captured, not just a safe check.
findings.promotion_notes: T4 = automatic replay of captured creds across the credential-spray loop (SSH, SMB, DB, cloud AKIA→STS). AKIA keys are recovered but stored with placeholder secret '(aws-access-key-id)' — needs paired SecretAccessKey mining or a T3 note to hunt the matching secret. Packfile support (delta resolution) would broadly widen coverage.
findings.tester_next_step: git-dumper https://<host>/.git ./loot; then trufflehog filesystem ./loot; also GitTools/Extractor.py to resolve packfiles. For any AKIA found: hunt paired `aws_secret_access_key` in same/nearby blobs; then aws sts get-caller-identity.
